rationales.quote: Is that just with like plaid or whatever

rationales.quote: those can do a decent job of like pulling in and categorizing expenses
rationales.explanation: He notes that existing consumer finance tools already provide some overlapping functionality, raising a product differentiation concern.

rationales.quote: what separates in the early days, the people who get it and engage
rationales.explanation: Charles asks which users meaningfully engage and change their behavior rather than merely signing up.

rationales.quote: Are there any business types that don't work in Investrio
rationales.explanation: He probes the operational scope of the product across different customer business types.

rationales.quote: how much effort is required by the end user to get to a good outcome?
rationales.explanation: Charles asks whether the product can deliver a useful result without requiring substantial user effort.

rationales.quote: How, how much do you think they can afford to put to work with you?
rationales.explanation: He asks about the revenue ceiling and willingness to pay within the target customer segment.

rationales.quote: I've invested in some companies that have targeted solopreneurs
rationales.explanation: Charles explicitly grounds his segmentation concern in prior investments targeting solopreneurs.

rationales.quote: people who are making money through this as their primary occupation, but it's actually not viable
rationales.explanation: He argues that the broad solopreneur population includes businesses that are not viable customers for a venture-backed product.

rationales.quote: if you're serious and you're really running a business, you realize like, A, I want the deductions and B, I don't wanna get audited
rationales.explanation: Charles identifies serious business operators as a segment with a concrete tax-related need and potentially greater willingness to pay.

rationales.quote: I'm out on this one mostly 'cause I feel like there's a segmentation set of work I'd wanna see done here
rationales.explanation: He explicitly declines to invest because the customer segmentation and corresponding monetization model remain insufficiently resolved.

rationales.quote: all of the people that you will interact with as a business owner, they all are comfortable with QuickBooks
rationales.explanation: Charles sees ecosystem-wide familiarity with QuickBooks as a barrier to replacing the incumbent.

rationales.quote: sometimes like, product lock-in comes because the other people in the ecosystem understand the input
rationales.explanation: He explains that ecosystem participants' familiarity with QuickBooks creates workflow lock-in that can impede adoption of a new product.

rationales.quote: You probably have to monetize those customers in ways that don't require them to actually pay you more money
rationales.explanation: Charles argues that the target customers' limited ability to pay requires an alternative monetization model.

rationales.quote: You need to be able to take that customer base and market it to somebody else
rationales.explanation: He proposes monetizing the customer base through another paying party rather than relying solely on direct subscription revenue.

rationales.quote: the customer she's going after has a actually like a very hard capped amount of money they can actually pay
rationales.explanation: Charles believes the target segment imposes a hard ceiling on direct customer revenue.

rationales.quote: there are lots of other alternative
rationales.explanation: He points to alternative monetization mechanisms as a possible way to make a low-price offering viable.

rationales.quote: you look at the solopreneurs number. And you're like, it's so many people. And then you start to slice it
rationales.explanation: Charles argues that the large headline solopreneur market becomes materially smaller when segmented by serious, economically viable customers.

rationales.quote: it's hard to get money from the casual people
rationales.explanation: He distinguishes serious business operators from casual solopreneurs who are unlikely to spend on the product.
